assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, turned laser-cooled atoms into clocks whose uncertainty is now near 1e-18. They let one measure time and gravitational redshift at the millimetre scale and test fundamental constants. This is precision atomic physics with clear conceptual content, and it is the kind of close theory-experiment agreement I value most.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and led the first demonstrations. Jun Ye's JILA group brought the strontium clock to the systematic-uncertainty frontier and the frequency-comb link. Two laureates is a clean configuration. Other groups (for example Lemonde and Le Targat in Paris, and Boulder NIST work on other species) contributed, and Hall and Hänsch were honoured for the comb in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories have reproduced and extended the clocks, and international comparisons and the redefinition of the second are under discussion. The field is mature and still improving, so recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit the optical-clock concept more broadly, including single-ion clocks (Wineland's 2012 prize already covers ion control).
I rely on memory for the detailed priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases and the Aharonov-Bohm effect change how we understand quantum states. Berry's 1984 phase underlies adiabatic transport, polarization, Berry curvature in solids and much modern topological physics. It is a deep, simple and unexpected insight about quantum mechanics itself, with consequences far beyond its origin.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are the main names. David Bohm is deceased and cannot share, which leaves two living laureates. Pancharatnam, Aharonov-Anandan and Simon are related contributions that the supplied credit does not include, so some attribution disputes remain.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades in optics, NMR, neutron interferometry and electron systems. The interpretation is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should cover the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase as one discovery or as distinct ones.
Priority questions around Pancharatnam and Aharonov-Anandan are not resolved in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling mechanical oscillators to their quantum ground state and demonstrating entanglement and squeezing of macroscopic motion speaks directly to where the boundary between quantum and classical lies. That question is, to me, among the most interesting in physics. The results are original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Cleland demonstrated quantum control of a mechanical resonator with superconducting qubits, while Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg developed the optomechanical cavity route and ground-state cooling. Teufel, Lehnert, Painter and Schliesser also made decisive contributions, so a three-person limit leaves some contested credit.
assessment.maturity: Several groups have confirmed these results independently. The field is maturing quickly and has links to gravitational-wave detectors and sensing. Slightly early in terms of consequences, but the core demonstrations are solid.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among a larger set of pioneers (Teufel, Painter, Lehnert, Schwab and others) is unclear.
The long-term importance of macroscopic quantum states depends on future tests of decoherence models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices, with the Mott-insulator transition and single-site imaging, give a controllable quantum many-body system whose Hamiltonian can be designed. This is a real conceptual advance for studying correlated matter and fits my AMO sympathies.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) proposed the Hubbard-model realization. Greiner, in Hansch's and Bloch's groups, observed the Mott transition, and Bloch led the single-site and quantum-gas-microscope programmes. Jaksch, Gerbier and others also contributed, and Cirac is in the supplied credit but I would choose three.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced and extended it, with reliable agreement between experiment and theory in appropriate regimes. The field is mature and still productive. The 2001 and 1997 laser-cooling and BEC prizes are the foundation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller entries on the longlist; the committee would need to decide how to split quantum simulation from quantum computation.
Whether quantum simulation has yet solved a problem inaccessible to classical computation is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a major new class of materials in which topology gives protected edge and surface states. The theory was unexpected and the experimental proof was clear. Condensed matter is outside my own specialty, so I defer in part to colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal, and Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Zhang is deceased, and Bernevig, Hughes, Fu, Moore, Hasan and others also contributed, so the split between theory and experiment is complicated.
assessment.maturity: The result has been confirmed repeatedly across materials, and the interpretation is stable. The field is mature enough for a prize.
uncertainties: The credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Hughes, Molenkamp, Fu, Moore and Hasan is genuinely contested.
The overlap with B012 shows the community is divided over how to frame the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observing the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model's mechanism for mass and was a landmark of experimental physics. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, but the experimental discovery is not yet honoured. I defer to colleagues on particle physics.
assessment.attribution: Recognition of collaborations of several thousand people is difficult. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS, but this credits project leadership more than the decisive analyses. Prize rules favour individuals, and this is a real tension.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and followed by measurements of couplings. Very mature, although the choice of laureates is the weak point.
uncertainties: Whether leadership credit can fairly stand in for a large collaboration's discoveries.
I am not expert in the detailed history of the discovery analyses.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links the foundations of quantum mechanics (entanglement, no-cloning, Bell tests) to secure communication. The BB84 and E91 protocols are original and clear. Part of the case rests on later technological application, which matters less to me than the fundamental insight.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard created BB84, and Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea complicates the history, and Wiesner is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are widespread, and commercial and satellite systems exist. Practical security depends on implementation and is still debated, but the theory is stable.
uncertainties: Priority of Wiesner and others, which the supplied credit cannot reflect.
Overlap with the long-distance communication entry B025 and the 2022 Bell-test prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BEC-BCS crossover in strongly interacting Fermi gases gives a universal, tunable system that links atomic physics to superfluidity in nuclear and neutron-star matter. The results are quantitative, and comparison with theory is strong.
assessment.attribution: Feshbach-resonance control and observation of molecular condensates and fermionic superfluidity were achieved by several groups (Jin, Grimm, Ketterle, Salomon, Thomas, Zwierlein). Deborah Jin died in 2016 and cannot share, which leaves a limited list of three of the living leaders.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent groups, and equations of state and the vortex evidence for superfluidity are well established. Mature, but allocation is hard.
uncertainties: Four named people compete for three places, with Jin deceased and Ketterle already honoured in 2001.
The overlap with the optical lattice and quantum simulation entries may dilute the case.
